name: mute-music
description: From the menu: open the settings window, switch music off, close it again.
note: Run it with game_run {routine:'mute-music'}. Steps are the game_input vocabulary plus {type:'command'} for a registered intent; `expect` holds the ordinary game_run predicates, ANDed and judged once after the last step. Only a STEP takes a `why` — an assertion is exactly the predicate object game_run takes, with no extra fields. The `toggled` expectation is the load-bearing one here: the box ships checked, so "it is off now" would also be true of a box nothing ever reached, while `toggled` fires only on a real state change and cannot be satisfied by a tap that bounced off a disabled control.

steps.name: open-settings
steps.why: The highest channel available: the SETTINGS button dispatches this intent, so the routine keeps working after any relayout of the menu — and the dispatch is journalled with the frame it happened on.

The scene's `settings.toggle-music` command FLIPS the box, so it cannot express "off" from an unknown state; setChecked can. It still goes through the control's own funnel, so the checkmark, the audio bus and the `toggled` signal all land exactly as they would on a tap.

steps.name: close-settings
steps.why: The CLOSE button's intent — same reason as opening.
